description.from:
Why: 55 of the 60 data models have no tenantId today (only Item, PublishedItem, MediaAsset, PublishedMediaAsset and NewsroomSection carry one; verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d (2026-11-08)). Six DynamoDB tables outside AppSync (newsletter, title-word index, public-form limits, reader and signup rate counters, remote-login) and the S3 Vectors index also have no tenant in their keys. This epic adds the tenant to every tenant-owned row and key, adds the new models a shared tier needs, and plans every index change around the one-new-index-per-table-per-deploy rule.

Answer to "does multi-tenant need big API schema changes?": no big change to the shape of existing queries and mutations. The changes are (1) additive: an optional tenantId on 55 models, six new models created as new tables, a few new operations; (2) a data change, not a schema change: index key VALUES that are global today get a "<tenant>#" prefix, so no new index is needed for them (Reference already has 15 indexes, 16 with PR #1239, against a default limit of 20 per table, so "one tenant index per existing index" is impossible anyway); (3) a few new indexes, one per table, only on tables where no index can reach all of one tenant's rows (decided by the inventory task); (4) two breaking steps, staged last: the authorisation rules (epic PPY-e0c34a) and making tenantId required on the shared stack. Full table: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md.

Done when: every tenant-owned row and key carries its tenant on the shared stack, adopt-tenant-data and copy-backend cover every model, and the GSI ledger check guards every release. Ends with a p.apyr.us page (via PPY-02227e).
